name: Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease Type 4D
aliases: Hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy Lom type

clinicalPearls: Autosomal recessive demyelinating neuropathy first described in the Roma (Gypsy) population of Lom, Bulgaria, hence the eponym HMSN-Lom; a founder NDRG1 variant underlies most cases.
The distinctive feature separating it from other demyelinating CMT is progressive sensorineural deafness developing from the second to third decade.
Childhood onset with distal weakness, wasting, foot deformity and early loss of deep tendon reflexes, followed by a slowly progressive course with prominent sensory loss.
Motor nerve conduction velocities are severely slowed in the demyelinating range, and by later life there is marked secondary axonal loss with distal amyotrophy.
Tongue atrophy and fasciculations may be seen, and some patients develop dysarthria as the disease advances.
Ask about ethnic background and consanguinity, as founder-effect testing for the common NDRG1 truncating variant can rapidly confirm the diagnosis.
Management is supportive: hearing aids or cochlear implantation for deafness, orthoses, physiotherapy and foot-deformity correction.
reference.pathophysiology: CMT4D results from biallelic loss-of-function variants in NDRG1 (N-myc downstream-regulated gene 1), classically a founder truncating variant prevalent in Roma communities. NDRG1 encodes a cytoplasmic protein highly expressed in Schwann cells that is implicated in intracellular trafficking, membrane protein recycling and stress responses, and appears essential for the maintenance rather than the initial formation of myelin. Loss of NDRG1 function impairs the Schwann cell's ability to sustain the myelin sheath and support the underlying axon, leading to a demyelinating and progressively axonal peripheral neuropathy. The same protein's role in cochlear and neural tissue accounts for the characteristic sensorineural hearing loss, distinguishing CMT4D from other autosomal recessive demyelinating neuropathies and linking the peripheral and auditory phenotypes to a shared defect in NDRG1-dependent cellular maintenance.
additionalDifferentials: CMT4C (SH3TC2) and other autosomal recessive demyelinating (CMT4) subtypes
CMT1A and dominant demyelinating CMT type 1
Other hereditary neuropathies with deafness (e.g. CMT associated with mitochondrial or connexin defects)
Refsum disease and other metabolic neuropathies with hearing loss
Acquired demyelinating polyneuropathy with unrelated sensorineural deafness
additionalInvestigations: Nerve conduction studies and electromyography demonstrating a demyelinating neuropathy with superimposed axonal loss
Targeted testing for the founder NDRG1 variant, or NDRG1 sequencing and gene panel where the founder allele is absent
Pure-tone audiometry and auditory brainstem responses to characterise sensorineural hearing loss
Sural nerve biopsy showing demyelination, onion-bulb formation and Schwann cell inclusions if genetics are unrevealing
Detailed family history with attention to ethnicity and consanguinity for founder-effect counselling
Speech and swallowing assessment where bulbar features emerge
redFlags: Progressive dysarthria or swallowing difficulty from bulbar involvement
Rapidly worsening hearing threatening communication and safety
Deterioration disproportionate to the expected slow course, prompting search for a superimposed acquired cause
Foot ulceration or injury arising from severe sensory loss
reference.prognosis: CMT4D causes progressive disability with loss of ambulation commonly by mid-adulthood, compounded by sensorineural deafness that usually becomes significant from young adulthood. The combined motor, sensory and auditory burden is disabling, though life expectancy is generally preserved.
pitfalls: Overlooking the diagnosis by not eliciting ethnic background, thereby missing rapid founder-variant confirmation
Attributing the hearing loss to an unrelated cause rather than recognising it as intrinsic to CMT4D
Assuming dominant inheritance and failing to counsel consanguineous families about recurrence risk
Delaying auditory rehabilitation because the neuropathy dominates the early clinical picture
references: International consensus guidance on inherited neuropathy classification
